requirements.quote:
The mailbox encoding standard
and mail exchange binding are part of the DNS official protocol, and are
the recommended method for mail routing in the Internet.
requirements.condition: When selecting a method for Internet mail routing.
requirements.required_behavior: Prefer the mailbox encoding standard together with mail exchange binding for mail routing; this is a recommendation.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected mail-routing method can be inspected for use of the recommended mailbox encoding and mail exchange binding.

requirements.quote:
The mailbox encoding standard assumes a mailbox name of the form
"<local-part>@<mail-domain>".
requirements.condition: When applying the mailbox encoding standard.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the mailbox name as a local part and a mail domain in the form <local-part>@<mail-domain>.
requirements.why_checkable: The mailbox encoder input decomposition can be inspected and tested with a local part followed by @ and a mail domain.

requirements.quote:
While the syntax allowed in each of these
sections varies substantially between the various mail internets, the
preferred syntax for the ARPA Internet is given in [RFC-822].
requirements.condition: For mailbox local-part and mail-domain syntax in the ARPA Internet.
requirements.required_behavior: Prefer the syntax given in RFC-822.
requirements.why_checkable: A syntax preference is stated, but the actual RFC-822 syntax constraints are not supplied in this chunk, so a concrete syntax check cannot be derived from this evidence alone.

requirements.quote:
The DNS encodes the <local-part> as a single label, and encodes the
<mail-domain> as a domain name.
requirements.condition: When encoding a mailbox name in DNS.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the entire local part as a single DNS label.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoder output can be checked to ensure that the local part occupies exactly one label, including when its text contains dots.

requirements.quote:
The DNS encodes the <local-part> as a single label, and encodes the
<mail-domain> as a domain name.
requirements.condition: When encoding a mailbox name in DNS.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the mail domain as a DNS domain name.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoder output for the mail-domain component can be inspected for a domain-name representation.

requirements.quote:
The single label from the <local-part>
is prefaced to the domain name from <mail-domain> to form the domain
name corresponding to the mailbox.
requirements.condition: When constructing the DNS domain name corresponding to a mailbox.
requirements.required_behavior: Prepend the single label encoding the local part to the domain name encoding the mail domain.
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting label sequence can be checked for the local-part label followed by the mail-domain labels.

requirements.quote:
If the
<local-part> contains dots or other special characters, its
representation in a master file will require the use of backslash
quoting to ensure that the domain name is properly encoded.
requirements.condition: When a mailbox local part contains dots or other special characters and its mailbox domain name is represented in a master file.
requirements.required_behavior: Use backslash quoting for the dots or other special characters in the local part so that the mailbox domain name is encoded correctly.
requirements.why_checkable: Master-file serialization and parsing can be checked to ensure that special characters are quoted and the local part remains one label.
